title: Champions League Predictions 10/21: Arsenal, Bayern, Real Madrid, Man Utd Feature
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 20, 2026Arsenal headline Wednesday’s fixtures. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesThe Champions League is really starting to find its groove after a slow start.

A three-week international break meant there was plenty of distance between Matchdays 1 and 2 of this season’s league phase, but we’re getting into the swing of things before national teams reconvene in November.

After Tuesday’s action threw up a barnstorming encounter between two of the favorites, Wednesday is supplying another heavyweight duel. Moreover, plenty of intrigue surrounds Vinícius Júnior‘s return to Real Madrid’s starting lineup amid a lengthy domestic suspension, as well as Manchester United’s trip to the idyllic Como.
The lack of jeopardy at this early juncture seems to liberate those competing, so expect another night of goalscoring mayhem as Matchday 3 concludes.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts Wednesday’s action to pan out.

Cesc Fàbregas and Michael Carrick are familiar foes. / Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesPrediction: Como 2–1 Man Utd
A “dream” night beckons for Cesc Fàbregas‘s Como on Wednesday evening, as the Champions League debutants welcome the mighty Manchester United to the Giuseppe Sinigaglia.

Michael Carrick’s Red Devils are hardly the imperious force they once were, and the visitors are set to be without a litany of players for this encounter. It’s a fixture Carrick can ill-afford to lose, given that United are six games without a win, yet he described Sunday’s draw at Leeds United as a "fresh start" after a week of several flashpoints.

Lisandro Martínez, who remained in the starting lineup at Elland Road despite his public outburst after last week’s defeat to Atlético Madrid, is among those unlikely to travel to Italy due to injury, as a depleted United aim to build on their gritty showing in West Yorkshire.
The burgeoning Como are seemingly everything their visitors are not in terms of alignment, and their Champions League bow on home soil last month was quite the occasion under the lights.

Barcelona were at least made to work for their eventual emphatic victory in Istanbul last week. At one point, it looked like Victor Osimhen had given Galatasaray a 2–0 lead, but the striker’s effort was ruled out for offside. Then came the onslaught.

The Turkish champions have exclusively relied on their home form for any success in this competition as of late, and will have to find a way of making themselves much harder to beat on their travels if they’re to show any signs of discernible progress on the continent.

A trip to Lille is hardly the most intimidating of away days, and Davide Ancelotti’s side hit a couple of stumbling blocks last week. After succumbing to a second-half Arsenal blitz on Matchday 2, Lille were held at home by Brest in Ligue 1 at the weekend.
Aston Villa had themselves a record-breaking night on their previous Champions League outing, thrashing Fenerbahçe 6–0.

After a poor opening month, Unai Emery’s new-look Villans are starting to click. They’ve won two of their previous three Premier League games, and the fresh additions are coming to the fore. Nicolas Jackson scored twice in last week’s rout, and Johan Manzambi was Villa’s match-winner at Newcastle United on Saturday.

Another kind home fixture on paper awaits, although Viking head into the bout off the back of their hugely admirable showing against Bayern Munich on Matchday 2. After losing comfortably at Stuttgart, Viking rallied after allowing a 2–0 lead to slip. Michael Olise’s red card aided their late revival, as Herman Haugen headed home a 90th-minute equalizer.
Bayern are unlikely to be the last team to suffer in Stavanger, but Viking will find it tough throughout the league phase to earn points on their travels.
Arsenal defeated the Bavarian giants in last season’s league phase. / Tom Jenkins/Getty ImagesPrediction: Bayern Munich 1–1 Arsenal
It’s the matchday of blockbusters. The Champions League’s ‘Barbenheimer.’
